claim: YES, a public 3D self-supervised representation model for Herculaneum CT exists: 'dinovol' (Vesuvius Challenge team, author Sean Johnson). It is a 3D adaptation of DINOv2 pretraining (DINO + iBOT + KoLeo losses, Gram anchoring, DINOv2/EVA-style ViT backbone, 3D RoPE positional encoding adapted from DINOv3, no absolute pos-emb) operating directly on voxel chunks of larger-than-memory OME-Zarr volumes. Code was first in github.com/ScrollPrize/dinovol (forked from bruniss/dinovol; 54 commits; archived read-only 21 Aug 2026 after being moved into the villa monorepo at github.com/ScrollPrize/villa/tree/main/dinovol). README states 'Pretraining works, but finetuning has not yet been implemented'. MIT license. v2 config example: 96^3 global / 48^3 local crops; HR-adaptation variants 128^3 and 160^3. Includes optional in-training task eval on 'surfaces' and 'ink' (mini U-Net decoders, 500 iters; ink: supervision_mask==0 ignored, unlabeled supervised voxels = background, max-projection over Z), point-supervised pretraining, and a napari visualizer (PCA / cosine-similarity of patch embeddings).
scan_compat: Input is 1-channel grayscale OME-Zarr CT at scale 0; README names no scroll, voxel size or keV. Released checkpoints (below) were trained on ~2.4 um ESRF BM18 volumes.

claim: How embeddings were turned into ink (arXiv:2606.29085 Methods + Suppl. Table 4, and HF card scrollprize/ink_3d_dino_guided): the Paris-4-finetuned dinovol ckpt (step 352,500) is run over 128^3 sliding windows (stride 128) giving 16^3 patch tokens per window, Gaussian-blended (sigma=4) and min-max normalised per 256^3 chunk. An expert clicked visibly inked voxels in axis-aligned slices; the mean of 256 clicked 864-D patch tokens, L2-normalised, is the 'ink prototype' (avg_ref_embedding.npy; recorded_embeddings.npy + recorded_embeddings_2.npy, 128x864 each). Cosine similarity to the prototype gives a dense 3D ink-likeness map. Labels = (frozen surface-conditioned ink-teacher probability x similarity S) > tau=0.5, with air/void masked (raw CT > 50 from round 2). A 3D residual-encoder nnU-Net-style U-Net (~142M params, 256^3 patches, 1-ch, sigmoid ink head; SGD Nesterov, cosine LR 1e-2, 5000-step warmup, bf16, Dice+BCE w/ 0.1 label smoothing, weight EMA) is trained as the 'DINO-guided student' (stage 2 of 4: teacher -> DINO-guided student -> background masking -> self-distillation from two guided checkpoints under TTA). Final released ckpt_78k_fullsup.pth (step 78,000) is the self-distilled model and no longer uses the DINO gate at inference. Trained on surface-conditioned labels from 8 scrolls (Paris 4, 0139, 0500P2, 0814, 0841, 1667, MAN5, 9B); the open-problems page says it is 'trained specifically for PHerc. Paris 4'. No quantitative ink metric for the DINO stage is given in the visible paper text ('reduced spurious DINO responses').

claim: Independent third-party audit (slchicoineau-creator/probeguide, 2026, undated; uses label set 20260918) of the DINO gate in villa's 3D ink pseudo-label recipe on PHerc. Paris 4 (8 labelled segments, proxy teachers PHerc.1667-iteration-0..5): the gate (teacher prob x cosine-sim-to-prototype > 0.5) keeps ~41% of true ink and ~18% of false ink but sits below the teacher's own PR curve; with a decent teacher (AUROC 0.86) the gate reduces AUPRC by 0.107 (p=0.016); a linear probe on dinovol tokens beats the prototype as a similarity map (within-chunk AUROC 0.59 -> 0.67) but no DINO variant improved a decent teacher within chunks.
